Classify interactions (Piggott et al. 2015)

Source: R/classify.R
classify_interactions.Rd

Codes the single, combined and interaction effects of each identifiable contrast set as positive, negative or not significant, and assigns the directional class of Piggott et al. (2015, Table 1) under the simple-addition (AD), multiplicative (MU), Bliss independence (BL), stress addition (SAM) and concentration addition (CA) null models.

Usage

classify_interactions(x, alpha = 0.05)

Arguments

x

A must_interactions object from estimate_interactions().

alpha

Significance level applied to the adjusted p-values (p_adjusted). Default 0.05.

Value

A data frame with one row per response, contrast set, sampling time and null model: response, context and the by columns, time, set_id, order, stressors, levels, background, null_model, scale, estimand ("net"), stressor_a, code_a, stressor_b, code_b (two-stressor sets only), single_codes (the code of every single effect, "salinity +; warming 0"), code_combined, code_interaction ("+", "-", "0", or "++" / "--" for the strong cases defined by Piggott et al.), pattern, class ("AD", "+S", "-S", "+A", "-A"), meaning, verdict (with an equivalence margin in estimate_interactions(): "deviation", "negligible", "equivalent" or "inconclusive"; NA otherwise), borderline (some adjusted p-value used is within two Monte Carlo standard errors of alpha, so that another seed could change the class), shared (the set shares cells with other sets), confounded (the set is confounded with differences among groups of units, see describe_design()), min_units, status ("ok", "not_applicable" or "not_estimable") and reason. The attribute alpha keeps the significance level, for report_interactions().

Details

Each effect is coded "0" if its adjusted p-value is at least alpha, and "+" or "-" after the sign of its estimate otherwise. A significant interaction is coded "++" ("--") when the combined effect is larger (smaller) than every single effect, or when the absolute interaction is larger than every absolute single effect (legend of Table 1 in Piggott et al. 2015), comparing point estimates on the scale of the null model. Table 1 then reduces to:

InteractionSingle effectsClass
0anyAD
++any+S
--any-S
+none negative+S
+at least one negative-A
-none positive-S
-at least one positive+A

Under MU, BL, SAM and CA, +S and -S mean "more positive" or "more negative" than the expectation of that null model, not than the sum of the single effects. The BL, SAM and CA classes are computed from the relative effects (w - 1) and the interaction of each model; the descriptive rescaled_class of estimate_interactions() is not used.

Three or more stressors. The net deviation of a set of k stressors is the combined effect minus the sum of the k single effects (AD, or the same on the log scale for MU), the comparison that Table 1 classifies; the same rules are applied with k single effects. This generalization is a design decision of this package: Piggott et al. (2015) define the classes for two stressors. The pure k-way interaction is not classified.

Verdicts. With an equivalence margin, the net interaction gets a verdict from its two adjusted p-values, both compared with alpha: "deviation" (deviation detected, not equivalent), "negligible" (a deviation detected but within the margin), "equivalent" (no deviation detected and within the margin) or "inconclusive" (neither). The class "AD" covers both "equivalent" and "inconclusive": only the first supports additivity (see "Equivalence" in estimate_interactions()). Combinations with only zeros have no test of equivalence, so their verdict is "deviation" or "inconclusive". DO interactions get a verdict too, although they have no class.

Combinations with only zeros (status = "boundary" in estimate_interactions()) are classified from the sign of their estimate (which may be infinite under MU) and their p-value.

Assumptions

  • AD means that no deviation from the null model was detected. It is not evidence of additivity: with few replicates most interactions will be classed AD. With a margin, verdict tells equivalent from inconclusive.

  • The class of a set with confounded = TRUE may reflect differences among groups of units (rooms, blocks) as much as the stressors.

  • The classification is defined for null models that predict the combination from the single effects (AD, MU, BL, SAM and CA). The dominance model gets status = "not_applicable", as do rows of "not_applicable" estimates (see sensitivity in estimate_interactions()).

References

Piggott, J. J., Townsend, C. R., & Matthaei, C. D. (2015). Reconceptualizing synergism and antagonism among multiple stressors. Ecology and Evolution, 5(7), 1538–1547. doi:10.1002/ece3.1465

Examples

jars <- expand.grid(
  salinity = c("ambient", "high"),
  warming = c("no", "yes"),
  replicate = 1:5,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
jars$jar <- seq_len(nrow(jars))
mu <- 40 * ifelse(jars$salinity == "high", 0.5, 1) *
  ifelse(jars$warming == "yes", 0.5, 1)
jars$algae <- stats::qpois(c(0.2, 0.35, 0.5, 0.65, 0.8)[jars$replicate], mu)
design <- describe_design(jars, c("salinity", "warming"),
  control = c(salinity = "ambient", warming = "no"), unit = "jar")
fits <- fit_responses(jars, "algae", design, residual_checks = FALSE,
  seed = 1, quiet = TRUE)
est <- estimate_interactions(fits, n_sim = 2000, seed = 1)
classify_interactions(est)
#>   response context time set_id order          stressors
#> 1    algae         <NA>    S01     2 salinity x warming
#>                        levels background null_model    scale estimand
#> 1 salinity=high | warming=yes                    AD response      net
#>   stressor_a code_a stressor_b code_b          single_codes code_combined
#> 1   salinity      -    warming      - salinity -; warming -             -
#>   code_interaction         pattern class
#> 1                + a - | b - | i +    -A
#>                                                            meaning verdict
#> 1 Combined effect less negative than the sum of the single effects    <NA>
#>   borderline shared confounded min_units status reason
#> 1      FALSE  FALSE      FALSE         5     ok
